findings.issue: Frame 0 shows the frontal mannequin face with a black band across the eyes (the fringe geometry) - it reads as a blindfold; her right hand floats in front of her chest with no visible forearm (a disembodied hand); the rattan case is lectern-sized (~0.8 m wide, standing to her chest) so she looks like she is at a podium, not sitting with a case across her knees.
findings.fix: Remove/reshape the fringe so no dark band crosses the eyes; open with her head bowed ~25 deg so the 2400K top light leaves the face in brow shadow, or crop the frame at the nose from frame 0. Re-pose the right arm: elbow out toward frame right, forearm visible, hand entering from upper right toward (0.40,0.62) as written. Scale the case to ~60x38x22 cm across her lap (lid ~0.55 m above the floor), knees visible under it; keep the folded-letter/front edge line at y 0.66 for T10.

findings.issue: Director note #1 is NOT fixed. The look back on 'xiang yin / chun bian' is a centred, sharp, flat front-lit mannequin head: the mask face fills ~55% of frame height, with a skull-cap hairline, a bare plastic ear, and the 'silent word' unreadable on a lipless mask. There is also a black gap all round the neck inside the mandarin collar, so the collar floats as a separate ring. The crowd 'flowing left to right behind her' is one blurred figure.
findings.fix: Re-stage it as a lost profile. Put the camera ~35 deg behind her right shoulder (100 mm, head ~35% of frame height at (0.62,0.38)), so we read the braid, the back of the head, the cheek line and the nose tip turning screen-left toward the farewell party. Move the 2400 K bulb to upper left behind her as a 3/4 back rim on the hair, cheek edge and braid. Take the frontal key down at least 2 stops, so the face is a dark shape with a warm edge against a brighter background: the blue twilight gate and the wet planks at ~2x the face luminance. Play the word at 112.33 as a small jaw/cheek movement in silhouette plus a visible breath. Close the collar gap (thicker neck or a collar that hugs it). Add 6-10 defocused travellers crossing left to right at 2-4 m, 1.0-1.2 m/s, so bokeh shapes sweep behind her for the whole shot.

findings.issue: 'Allowed to leave, but not yet to let go' has no movement. She stands still beside the case from frame 0. The two arms are already straight at the first frame (the S38_DMAX clamp lets her gain only ~0.5 m), so nothing 'pulls straighter' at 128.23. The case sits on the bottom frame edge and reads as set down, not carried. The barrier swing is not visible. An orange stick in the joined hands is an unexplained prop.
findings.fix: Start her ~0.5 m nearer the elder: left elbow bent ~90 deg, clasp at chest height ~1.15 m. Walk her 1.0-1.2 m toward the gate over 126.2-128.2, the case swinging in her right hand with air under it (tilt the camera down 3 deg or frame looser at the bottom), and have both arms reach full extension exactly at 128.23. Her look back at ~127.6. Track the camera ~0.8 m right with her, plus light handheld. Show the barrier leaf swinging at frame right from 126.19. Remove the stick, or make it the S034 sweets packet, legibly.

findings.issue: The emigrant crowd reads as a squad of near-identical uniformed men in peaked caps standing in blocks toward the gate. That reads as police, soldiers or conscription, not a migrants' departure, and it changes the meaning of the farewell. The brief's 'crowd flowing' (人群流动) is also absent in S032.
findings.fix: Rebuild the crowd as mixed civilians: flat caps or bare heads, headscarves, a mother with a child, bundles on shoulders, baskets, trunks. Heights 1.5-1.8 m; indigo, grey, brown and faded print clothing; irregular spacing and walking speeds (0.8-1.3 m/s). Keep at most 1-2 uniformed clerks, at the gate only. Reuse the same crowd set in S032 (defocused) and S036/S038.

findings.issue: Director note #7 is NOT fixed. pier_waiting still sets the engine grain to 0 and draws its own half-res grain quad (GRAIN 0.044, LOWRES layer), although the engine grain is now an integer PCG hash. The half-res grain is coarser (2x2 px clumps) and luminance-weighted differently, so the grain texture visibly changes across the T13 (S030->S031) and T15 (S039->S040) match cuts, which are exactly where the eye compares the two frames.
findings.fix: Remove grainQuad and grainProbe and the 'p.grain = 0' override. Return grain: 0.04-0.044 (bible CT_MIG) through the engine post. Verify by flipping S039's last frame against S040's first frame at 200%.

findings.issue: The S035->S036 'light' transition (niche lamp -> warm row of steamer portholes) does not connect. The lamp is at (0.15,0.47); the portholes are white, in three rows across x 0.52-0.78, and the brightest point in S036 is an overhead bulb clipped at the top edge (0.73,0.02). The steamer has no hull, funnel or masts and reads as an office block. The 'foreground hands come into focus' at 121.41 cannot happen: the clasp is mid-ground and ~3% of the frame.
findings.fix: Make the steamer a dark hull silhouette against the twilight: one row of warm 2000 K portholes at y ~0.40, a sparse second row on the superstructure, a funnel and masts. Make those portholes the brightest, warmest points in the frame. Dim the overhead bulb 50% or tilt it out of frame. Move the camera ~1.5 m closer along the railing (or lower and left) so the clasped hands sit in the foreground at ~10-12% of frame height at (0.30,0.62), with the gate and steamer deep beyond.

findings.issue: The migrant's sleeve changes. In the close-ups (S039's right arm, S037's soft left edge) it is a dark grey check/tweed; in S032/S036/S038 it is the faded floral blouse (lock: 褪色碎花布衫). In S039 both hands are the same smooth terracotta and evenly front-lit: nothing says the elder's hand is old, and the specified backlight through the finger gaps (逆光) is missing.
findings.fix: Use the floral blouse sleeve in every shot. Give the elder's hand an older read: darker, visible knuckles and tendons, slightly loose skin texture. Make the migrant's hand lighter and smoother. Put the key behind the hands from the blue gate (rim plus translucency between the fingers), front fill -1 stop.

findings.issue: The stamp lifts late. At 125.6 (frame 3014) it is still pressed, and the violet mark shows only in the last ~0.3 s before the cut at 126.125, too short to register before S040 rhymes it. The clerk's left fingernails render white-tipped (a French-manicure look), in focus under the bulb. The soft grey-checked cylinder at the left edge (her sleeve) fills ~18% of frame width and reads as an unidentified object.
findings.fix: Lift the stamp 125.35-125.6 so the mark holds for at least 0.5 s (12 frames). Use plain short nails on the clerk's hand and show the khaki cuff. Make the left-edge sleeve the floral blouse and crop it to x < 0.10.

findings.issue: 'The elder closes her fingers over the sweets' reads stiffly. The migrant's two forearms enter from the right edge as parallel straight tubes about 40% of frame width long, with no sleeve. The oil-paper packet reads as a glowing gold brick: hard edges, uniform emission, no red string cross, nothing visible through the paper.
findings.fix: Bend her elbows and bring the cupped hands toward her lap, so the forearms enter diagonally from bottom right and are cropped at x ~0.85, with the floral sleeve hems at the wrists. Make the packet soft crumpled translucent paper: emission ~50%, the red string cross clearly visible, darker sweet shapes showing through.

findings.issue: The keepsake is hidden. At 116.29 her right palm covers ~80% of the red-brown bundle, so the comb never registers, though it is the object the next 60 s builds on (S030, S043). Her left hand floats mid-air beside the case for ~1.5 s with nothing to do, and the opening of the lid is not readable.
findings.fix: Press the bundle with two fingertips at its edge so 70% of the faded red-brown cloth shows (comb outline visible through it), placed at the shirt's top centre. Have the left hand hold the raised lid edge at the top of frame from 115.33.

findings.issue: CH2's new detail - the cloth triangle in the repeatedly folded letter - is unreadable. The 'letter' is a flat cream card ~6% of frame width that never unfolds; the cloth is a grey smudge on it (140.22); she never visibly opens, strokes or refolds anything - two detached mitten forearms pat a card on a lid. The rattan suitcase 'across her knees' reads as a 70 cm crate / lectern filling the lower half. Frame 0 shows her frontal mannequin face with the black band across the eyes (Q1's S020 fault repeated; director note #1). The S043->S044 match only works because the case's lid edge (y 0.63-0.68) happens to sit at the ruler height - the letter fold, the registered element, plays no part.
findings.fix: Keep S020's camera data (the repeat) but open at S020's END framing and push to ~1.4x by 140.2 so the top of frame cuts at her nose - no face, braid and bowed head-top only at upper left. Scale the case to bible size (~50x33x17 cm) lying on her thighs, top surface at y~0.70. 139.9-140.22 the letter unfolds visibly (two folds lifting) to ~22% of frame width at (0.52,0.62); the cloth triangle #6F7F8F, 3x4 cm (~5-6% of frame width), lifted 1 cm by her right thumb at 141.18 so the 2400K bulb rims it; hold 0.4 s; refold on the old creases and press with the palm by 141.8 so the folded top edge is the clean horizontal at y=0.66, x 0.34-0.66 (S044 register). Use hi hands with articulated fingers; forearms continuous with the blouse sleeves.

findings.issue: Director note #6 is NOT fixed. The 'small tender handover of the sweet' is two arms held straight out at shoulder height meeting mid-frame like a handshake or arm-wrestle (f5176, f5183 at 215.94): she grips his wrist and the sweet is invisible. At 216.6 her other arm sticks out toward his lap. The 'nervous boy' reads as a broad adult man (same size as her, big frontal mannequin face under the cap), and both faces are lit frontal masks. There is a specular hot spot on her hair at (0.18,0.24). The S067->S068 'giving direction' match has no motion at the cut (S067 ends static).
findings.fix: Hand-over at lap height. Her right hand travels low from the packet in her lap (0.32,0.66) to his palm resting open on his bundle (~(0.60,0.68)): elbow bent ~90 deg, wrist turned up, the 2x3 cm amber brittle pinched between thumb and two fingers and visible against his palm. His hand stays low and cupped, not raised, and closes after 215.94. No arm above y 0.60. Her left hand stays on the packet. Boy: scale ~0.9 with narrower shoulders, cap brim lowered so the overhead 2400K bulb leaves his eye sockets in shadow; both faces in 3/4 profile toward each other, her smile carried by a head tilt. Raise hair roughness to kill the hot spot.

findings.issue: The OUTRO's dawn is not monotonic and the S076->S077 match cut jumps 1.3 stops back to night. Mean luminance: S075 24-28% -> S076 44.8% (warm, RGB 124/111/111) -> S077 17.8% (night-blue) -> S078 31% -> S079 27-30% -> S081 32 -> 45%. S076's hazy, warm, high-key morning already matches the final shot's brightness and warmth, which pre-empts the film's last image ('dawn warmth only at the end') and makes the return to the modern window feel like going back into the night. Her face is also an evenly lit profile mask, and her right arm is stretched at full length along the rail (0.45-0.75, 0.9).
findings.fix: Bring S076 down ~0.9 stop (mean ~26%) and cool it: blue-grey P20 haze with only a thin cool-peach band at the right horizon and light from screen-right as a soft gradient on her profile edge (rim), face plane ~1 stop under the haze, so she reads as a profile silhouette in mist like S075. Bend her elbow so the right hand rests on the rail near her body (x ~0.45). S077 is raised separately (see S077) so the chain climbs ~26 -> 26 -> 28 -> 30 -> 32-45%.

findings.issue: The fingertip gesture match is loose and S012's action does not read. S011 ends with small fingertip pads at ~(0.50,0.45-0.55), fingertip ~12% of frame height; S012 opens on a glove ~3x larger whose fingertips are at ~(0.45,0.64), pointing nearly vertical. S012 holds a half-bowl (the boat side), not a rim shard, the second shard is not visible, nothing joins on '碎' (57.2 s), and the sleeve comes out of a black cylinder.
findings.fix: Change the S012 side: frame 0 at the S011 registration (glove index pad at (0.50,0.52), fingers along the same 30 deg diagonal from upper right, fingertip ~12% of frame height), then ease out to the CU. Make the held piece a ~5 cm rim shard pinched between thumb and index; second shard on grey foam at lower left; on 57.2 s the held shard seats into the other (2-frame settle), the crack closing between two plum blossoms. Sleeve with folds; left forearm on the bench edge as written.

findings.issue: A 'same object, push in' cut drops a full stop and flips colour: S012 end mean 91/255 warm 3500K -> S013 frame 0 mean 45/255, blue-grey, with the shard in shadow. Later in S013 a blown specular bloom sits at the upper left like a lens-flare blob.
findings.fix: Start the slider inside the lamp's raking pool: rotate the shard (or move the lamp) so the crack's first 0.5 s is under the 3500K light, warm, with the cool window only as fill on the far side; frame 0 mean within ~0.3 stop of S012's end. Raise specular roughness or the bloom threshold for this shot so the glaze highlight is a highlight, not a flare.

findings.issue: The lab MCU exposes the mannequin: a fully lit pink profile face with a strapped black loupe; her out-of-focus right arm is a grey tube crossing ~70% of the frame to the ledger; the shard in her left glove reads as a black disc, so '翻过残片看圈足 -> 写下日期' does not read.
findings.fix: Camera over her right shoulder, 3/4 back, 50 mm at ~1.1 m: the shard and loupe are the subject, her face in lost profile (cheek/ear edge only). Put the 3500K lamp behind the shard toward camera-right so the porcelain is the brightest thing in frame and the foot ring's 火石红 catches warm; her right forearm rests along the bench below frame and the pencil enters lower right on 62.82. If the current angle is kept: face key to ~25% and lamp as a rim from frame right; pull the right arm back out of frame.

findings.issue: T07 lands on position and scale (rim centre ~(0.50,0.52), diameter ~77-80% of height on both sides) but not on pattern: S015 is shot straight down and the rim is plain white; S016's rim is a bright silver halo ring around the rice. The plum band - the reason for the match ('相同花纹的碗') - is invisible on both sides.
findings.fix: S015 (this module): tilt 15 deg from vertical from the 6 o'clock side as written, so the outer plum band reads along the near lip (~y 0.86-0.90) with the window motif below it. old_home S016 frame 0: the identical tilt so the same band reads at 6 o'clock under the rice, and cut the rim specular/bloom so the cobalt band is visible instead of a steel-like halo.

findings.issue: BR1's emotional pivot ('也读我没说完的喜欢' - she reads the person, not the date) is not delivered. Instead of the paper-level ECU with a rack from the jasmine to her eye, the whole shot (170.21-174.58) is a static high three-quarter wide of the restorer hunched over the bench: her warm-lit mannequin face (bald-reading cap, nose, cheek) fills the top third, the magnifier is held upright like a lollipop beside her face (her eye is never behind the lens), the jasmine is invisible (<1% of frame), the right glove is a featureless white lump, the left arm lies flat as a plank, and there is no focus move at 172.14-172.92. The spectral ring appears on the paper at (0.75,0.69) instead of (0.72,0.30), so the light-to-light cut into S055 (lancet's brightest cluster upper-right) does not connect.
findings.fix: Rebuild to the keyframe: 100 mm, lens 3-4 cm above the blotter at the letter's near edge, looking up across the sheet toward her. Bottom band: jasmine + the broken stroke soft-sharp at (0.42,0.88), >=10% of frame width. Her face 0.30-0.35 m beyond, three-quarter, keyed only by the lowered 3500K lamp as top/edge light (keep >=70% of the face below 0.15 luminance; no frontal fill) so the mask never reads. 170.82 the magnifier slides in between flower and lens (rim ~35% of frame height, her gloved fingers on the handle at lower right). 172.14->172.92 rack focus from 0.06 m to the eye through the lens (f/2): the magnified eye (mole below the LEFT eye at the lens edge) becomes the sharpest thing at (0.52,0.42) on '欢'. 174.3 tilt the magnifier 15 deg so the pastel ring (muted ruby/amber/cobalt) lands at (0.72,0.30) and hold 6 frames into the S055 cut. Gloved fingertips hover 5 mm above the paper, never touching.

findings.issue: '原来还有这个' - the jasmine reads as an orange-brown burn/rust stain (~3% of frame) with a hooked stroke, not a pressed flower. The front of the letter carries crisp, high-contrast pseudo-hanzi that look like real-but-wrong characters (ruling 4: letters stay illegible/soft; to a Chinese audience these read as gibberish). The sheet flips as a rigid board around a vertical axis. The glove drops to blue-grey in shadow (continuity with the warm-white gloves of S049).
findings.fix: Model the pressed jasmine: 5-7 translucent overlapping browned petals (#A88A5A), ~2.5 cm -> >=8% of frame height at (0.58,0.46), raking lamp from upper left giving a hairline shadow and petal translucency; keep the broken last column immediately beside it (ruling). Defocus the front text (focus plane on the back margin, f/2.8) or halve its stroke contrast and blur the texture 1.5 px. Curl the sheet as it turns (>=20 deg bend, vertex curl or 3-segment hinge) over 165.9-166.4. Add a warm 2800K bounce so the glove stays warm-white (#E9E4DA) in shadow.

findings.issue: She never lifts her eyes: the head stays bowed through 160.92 ('看穿：她抬眼，若有所思') to the end, so the line '读过年月，不等于把你看穿' has no face to land on. Her right arm is a rigid straight tube reaching ~70 cm to the ledger (plank pose); the letter she is reading is not in frame (only the ledger). At 960 px her ear (dark concha, bright rim) reads as a black earbud - an unwanted 'she is listening to music' read. The flashlight sweep in the door pane at ~160.6 does read - keep.
findings.fix: 160.92-161.6 head lifts 12-15 deg and turns ~10 deg toward frame right past the lamp (not toward the door), held to 162.5, pencil frozen mid-air; keep the face in the current low-key side light (the lift should reveal only brow/eye-socket edge). Bend her right elbow ~100 deg, forearm along the bench edge, hand at (0.64,0.82); left forearm in the foreground with the worn cuff spot (keyframe). Put the letter (out of its sleeve) flat in the lamp pool at lower centre, soft. Lighten the ear's interior albedo and soften its rim so it reads as skin.

findings.issue: The aged handle reads NEWER than the new one: S049's is a smooth brown wooden dowel while S048's has a textured rattan wrap - the 'same object, decades later' ageing is inverted. The case opening happens off-camera (155.7-156.0) and the '15 deg tilt' reads as a cut from a side view to a top-down view. Contents are flat abstract slabs: a red square with a yellow half-disc (comb), a flat grey board (the shirt). Director note #5 only partly fixed.
findings.fix: Old handle = S048's rattan-wrap geometry with dark-brown sweat-stained albedo, frayed fibre ends, a broken binding at the right; the same lit position y=0.66. Show the lid lifting on its far hinge 155.6-156.3 while the camera tilts smoothly 15 deg (no framing jump). Comb: boxwood #C9A36A with visible teeth on the red-brown cloth, moved aside to the left; shirt: folded grey-blue cloth with fold lines, collar and one button; polyester sleeve with a clear edge highlight when lifted at 157.02.

findings.issue: S051 frame 0 is near-blown cream (mean 186/255) straight after S050's 22 - a 3-stop flash on the cut - then drops to ~116 as the lamp contracts; the keyframe wants deep blue-black edges from frame 0. The faded vermilion column rule is missing, so the last line reads as a row of ticks.
findings.fix: Open S051 already at the contracted-pool level (mean ~110-120, vignette to deep blue-black at the edges) or move the lamp-pull into S050's last 0.3 s; add the faded vermilion rule (#B4533F) running left-right under the column.

findings.issue: The restorer's faint reflection lands exactly on the empty bench across from the wife (~(0.62,0.42)), seated, hands resting on the table: it reads as a second person sitting opposite her for the whole shot (f1608-f1692). That destroys PRE1's core image (对面的座位始终空着 / 一夜未眠). The home is also tiny (wife ~20% of frame height), so her breathing at 69.6 s does not read.
findings.fix: Move her reflection off the bench: reflected head+shoulder at ~(0.82,0.30), larger than the home figures (head ~18% of frame height: she is nearer the glass), partly cut by the right muntin, warm 3500K rim distinct from the candle, >=4 px soft once focus goes deep - or put it over the left wall above the wife. Keep the right bench visibly empty with the bowl and chopsticks in the lattice moonlight. Push in (100 mm or dolly ~30%) so the wife is ~35% of frame height and the shoulder rise at 69.6 s reads.

findings.issue: On '失' (66.32 s) the pull-back is meant to reveal the empty bench; it never does - at 66.32 and at the end frame only the candle and the bowl show, the right edge is a dark plank. With S017 broken too, the empty seat is never established in PRE1. The WIFE's hands at the left edge read as a segmented orange-wood artist's manikin hand, and the bangle is cut off.
findings.fix: Extend the rise/pull so the empty bench occupies the right ~22% (x 0.78-1.0), its edge lit by the lattice moonlight, by 66.32; bowl+chopsticks at ~(0.65,0.55) in front of it. Hands: skin material (desaturated #C9A88A), folded right over left, the silver bangle on the LEFT wrist at ~(0.08,0.62) catching the candle - or crop the hands out and let S017 introduce her.

findings.issue: The chorus's single action (empty bowl set under the eave on '等', 74.18 s) is unreadable at screen size: the crouched woman is ~12% of frame height and the bowl ~2.5% of frame width; the S019->S020 right-hand gesture match therefore has nothing to match. The door jamb glows as an orange neon outline. The sky fills the right half to the sea horizon rather than the top third, and it is brighter than S018's end sky (117 vs 138/255 top-right) with a different cloud pattern, so the sky match from S018 is weak.
findings.fix: Dolly in (or 50 mm) so the woman is ~40-45% of frame height and the bowl >=5% of frame width at ~(0.30,0.78), on the step's outer edge under the drip line, with a moon specular on the glaze; her right hand lifting off the rim on 74.6 reads in the lower-middle region for the S020 hand-off. Door: soft 1850K candle spill on threshold and step, dim the jamb edge. Sky: use S018's shared sky plate B, grade it ~0.3 stop down to S018's end; keep the moon at (0.80,0.14). (Setup is reused in S041.)

findings.issue: The reflection transition jumps scale at the same screen position. The S040 glove is ~38% of frame height wide, about 76% tall, at (0.36,0.56). S041's frame 0 shows the same glove at ~11% wide on a much wider lens, plus a coat sleeve: a 3.8x pop that reads as a zoom jump cut, not 'focus passing through the glass'. S040 is T15-locked to S039, so S041 is the side to change.
findings.fix: Start S041 on S040's exact framing (glove width ~38% of frame height at (0.36,0.56), same soft permit glow behind). Over 0.6-1.2 s pull focus through the glove into the reflection while the glove drifts soft off the bottom-left; the eaves resolve behind it, then lock. If the wide S019-matching composition must arrive sooner, use an 8-frame dissolve instead of a 0-frame 'reflection'.

findings.issue: 'Mending with a shy smile' does not read. The turned-out indigo cuff is a rigid black basket-weave cylinder held up at the chest, which reads as a purse or a cup sleeve, not a sleeve. There is no visible needle or thread. The lower face (nose, mouth, jaw) is front-lit full by the candle, exposing the mask, where the spec asks for side-back light with half the face in shadow. Her look toward the left doorway at 119.5 does not happen (her head stays down), so the focus pull to the niche lamp has no motivation. The bangle and thimble are not readable. This patch is the key continuity link to the navigator's cuff (S011/S045).
findings.fix: Make the cuff soft indigo cotton with drape and a turned-back hem, not basket weave. Lay the pale-blue patch flat on it with visible stitches, and add a needle and thread catching the candle (1-2 px highlight). Lower the work to lap height. Move the candle key side-back to frame right, so only the mouth corner, chin and cheek edge catch light. At 119.5 turn her head 20-25 deg toward frame left (0.3 s), then rack to the niche lamp 119.8-120.31. Brighten the silver bangle on the left wrist and the brass thimble on the left middle finger.

findings.issue: The 'reflection' hand-off is a hard on-axis jump cut: S040 ends on the glove ~60% of frame height at (0.37,0.58); S041 opens on the same glove ~22% of frame height at (0.36,0.55) - a ~2.7x scale jump on the same subject. The glove then floats on a straight vertical black sleeve (puppet-stick arm, orange cuff band) beside a large defocused warm blob (G3c case glow) that owns the centre for ~1 s.
findings.fix: Change S041's opening (the incoming side): start on S040's last-frame scale and angle (glove ~60% frame height at (0.37,0.58), sleeve entering from lower-left at ~35 deg), slightly soft, then over 135.42-136.4 rack focus into the reflection while the glove's opacity goes to 0 - no reframe. Drop the G3c glow 2 stops or move it off-centre so the eaves image reads by 135.48 ('千年啊').

findings.issue: Locked CH2 frame: the empty bowl - the object that carries the cut into S042 and the 'waiting for rain' idea - is a 1-2% white speck; the right half of the 2.39 frame is a flat, featureless grey 'cloud' plane over a flat sea, so the CH2 weather change (heavier, lower cloud, damp stone) reads as fog on a wall rather than weather. The wife sits on a dark block rather than the doorstone.
findings.fix: Give the bowl a small pool of door/niche spill so it is the brightest small highlight left of her, or move it 0.4 m toward camera so it reads >=3% of frame width at (0.28,0.80); give the cloud deck structure (darker bellies, a lit edge around the moon glow, 2-3 layered bands moving slowly), a faint glitter path on the sea under the glow; wet the step (roughness ~0.25, a dark damp edge) and add 2-3 eaves drips. Seat her on the doorstone (no block).

findings.issue: The child's entrance is awkward: at 139.0 (f3336) a foot slides in horizontally at mid-height like a floating limb, then two legs drop from the top edge like pillars; shins run to the top of frame (spec: nothing above the ankles), which makes the child read adult-tall; at 139.68 the toes poke out BELOW the sole line (clipping into the stone). The rim band of the canonical bowl, at its largest in CH2, reads as isolated dots rather than one continuous plum branch.
findings.fix: Step in from behind/above the threshold: heel lands first at (0.50,0.70) on 139.02 from ~5 cm above, foot travel <=12 frames, soles never shown to camera. Flag the door light so shins above ~8 cm fall into darkness (or tilt 6 deg down) - only feet and ankles read. Toe group sits on the stone (+2 mm), and the 139.68 wiggle is a 3-4 mm curl of the toes, not a sub-sole pop. Paint the rim band as a continuous branch linking the blossoms (bible PROP_BOWL).

findings.issue: Director note #2 not fixed for S021: the diagonal louvre stripes still dominate the whole frame, the map is unreadable, the ruler is a matte black slab, and the wet ink line is a thin dark hair barely visible above it - so the S020->S021 line match (letter edge -> ink line at y 0.66) does not land and '握在掌间' has no map to hold.
findings.fix: Stripe contrast <=1.6:1 and confine them to the upper-right ~40% (across the sea part of the map); the line zone y 0.55-0.80 lit by the 2200K kerosene lamp only. Ruler: ebony sheen + a brass edge highlight. The ink line on the drawing edge at y 0.66 with a wet specular that travels with the pen; pen hand above the ruler.

findings.issue: Director note #2 is NOT fixed. About 33 hard-edged louvre stripes at full contrast (~8:1) cover the whole frame, and the map underneath is unreadable blotches. The coastline is a 1-2 px squiggle that reads as a hair or crack. The ink line is a 1-2 px hairline on top of the ruler, with no wet blue-black sheen, so 'shan he' has no visible action. The ebony ruler is a pure-black bar ~9% of frame height, the largest shape in frame, and reads as a redaction bar. At 'zhang' (79.64) the left arm comes from the bottom centre across the ruler and the fresh line to press at upper right, crossing over the pen hand (arms crossed, and his sleeve lies on wet ink; the S044 ruling says the palm is never on wet ink).
findings.fix: Cut the louvre contrast to at most 1.6:1. Widen the pitch to ~10 stripes across the frame, soften the edges (penumbra ~1/3 of the pitch), and fade them toward the upper left, so the lower half (ruler, line, coast) is keyed by the 2200 K kerosene lamp from frame right. Make the ruler ~3.5% of frame height: ebony with brass edges that catch the lamp, so its drawing edge at y 0.66 is a bright line. Draw the ink 4-6 px wide at 960 px, blue-black, with a specular highlight that travels with the nib. Paint the map as a 3-4 px sepia coast with hachures, sea washed grey-blue on the left, land warm paper on the right, and a clear village dot and ring at (0.30,0.58). At 79.64 the left hand leaves the ruler and presses flat on the land BELOW the ruler at (0.58,0.86), with the forearm entering from the bottom edge, so it never crosses the line or the pen hand.

findings.issue: Both cuts that S021 sits between match weakly. IN: S020's strongest horizontal is the lit case edge at y 0.65 (bright), while S021's is a pure-black ruler bar at y 0.66-0.75. The shape matches but the tone is inverted, and the registered subject (the folded letter edge, ~60% width) is a tiny strip under her hands. OUT: the village mark (0.29,0.59) lines up with S022's shore light (0.30,0.58), but the map's coast runs vertically through the frame while the real coast in S022 is a horizontal silhouette at y 0.58, x 0-0.48. S021's final 0.6 s also leaves the eye on the pressing hand at upper right (0.65,0.25), far from where the light appears.
findings.fix: S021 is the cheaper side to change. With the brass-edged ruler from the S021 readability finding, the drawing edge becomes a bright line at y 0.66, which matches S020's lit edge. Redraw the coast so it runs horizontal at y 0.58 from x 0 to 0.30, then turns down to cross the ruler at x 0.30. That keeps 'from the sea into the land' and mirrors S022's coastline. In the last 8-10 frames (80.0-80.29), run the kerosene glint along the wet ink back to the crossing point (0.30,0.62) and keep the palm below the ruler, so the eye is on (0.30,0.58) when the shore light appears. Optional, pier_waiting: end S020's push-in tighter so the folded letter edge spans at least 35% of the width.

findings.issue: Note #7: map_office still adds an in-scene grain quad (setGrain 0.14-0.18), drawn before DOF and tonemapping, with the engine grain at 0. Its texture and level differ from the neighbouring modules.
findings.fix: Remove grainQuad/setGrain and use the engine grain (0.035-0.04) like the neighbouring shots.

findings.issue: Director note #2 NOT fixed. In S044 and S047 the louvre moon-stripes are still ~60/40 hard white bands across the whole frame, brighter than the map; the coastline is a heavy black hair-like squiggle; S047's hachures still read as animal fur at 100 mm; the new ink line is a matte black rod with a dotted highlight (not wet iron-gall ink); the pen reads as a white plastic tube; S047's lower 30% is a dead black slab (ruler body). S044 end: black marks on the pressed fingernails (map decal showing through the nails) and the spread fingers are cut by the top edge, palm centre ~(0.47,0.42) instead of (0.45,0.60). The village (the 'new detail') is rows of tiny boxes that only half-read under the stripes.
findings.fix: Stripes: contrast <=1.3:1 (moon-through-louvre x0.3, penumbra x3 so slats are soft bands), make the 2200K lamp from frame right the key. Paper: replace the hachure texture with sparse printed 0.2 mm strokes at ~15% opacity, fibre only as a low-amplitude (<=0.1) normal; coastline 0.4 mm sepia at 50%; village houses drawn as tiny pitched roofs + boats, darker than the hachures. Ink: 1.0-1.2 mm blue-black line with a clearcoat/specular strip catching the lamp for ~0.8 s behind the nib, a hair of bleed. Nib: steel (metalness 1, roughness 0.25). S047: drop the ruler to y>=0.80 (line stays at 0.66) and give its brass edge + ebony a lamp highlight so the lower third isn't black. S044: end with palm centre (0.45,0.60), fingertips >=0.06 below the top edge, hand width ~35-40% of frame height (also the S045 register); lift the nail geometry 1 mm or draw the decal with polygonOffset so nothing prints through the hand.

findings.issue: The cross-era hand match does not match: S044 ends on a spread hand ~0.8 frame-heights wide, fingers to the top edge, mean 69/255 with white stripes; S045 opens on a hand ~0.55 wide pointing down-left, mean 14/255. Scale, orientation and a 2.3-stop exposure drop make it a jarring cut, not a match.
findings.fix: Change the S044 side (already under rework): stop the push so the hand is ~35-40% of frame height wide at (0.45,0.60), palm down, fingers toward frame top; with softened stripes S044's end should sit near mean 40. In S045 orient his left hand the same way at frame 0 (wrist toward the lower edge, fingers toward the top, palm down onto the cuff) and lift to mean ~30 (see S045).

findings.issue: The hand does not grip: a mitten-like fist rests on top of the handle bar, fingers never curl around it, and nothing tightens at 154.4 ('关'); note #6 scale is now OK. The mid-tilt frames 153.4-153.8 are unreadable (a doubled threshold line, a floating shoe over a second floor). The two shoes merge into one large black blob at frame 0.
findings.fix: Fingers wrap under the bar (2nd-5th fingers' tips hidden behind it, knuckles on top, thumb over the index), small hand per bible; at 154.4 a 2-3 mm squeeze with knuckle highlights +20% (whitening). Tilt path: rise along her side (skirt hem -> blouse hem -> hand) with focus following, a single threshold line. Separate the shoes (10 cm apart, one slightly ahead) so they read as a pair side-on.

findings.issue: The ruling's beat (phone light dies at 190.6; she sees only an unlit bent back) never happens. The phone is lowered out of the bottom edge at ~190.3 (f4566-4570) and the last 0.6 s is a bright warm sill + window pillar with his empty open hand; the face-down phone on the thigh is never seen. The end frame (mean 43/255) is brighter than the start (38) and twice S061's first frame (21) - there is no darkness to move her. Continuity: the phone is a modern slab with a chrome-blue bezel highlight, not the old dark-grey phone in a worn navy flip case with a cracked corner (bible 6.17); at 188.71 his thumb lies ON the screen instead of hovering over the dial key.
findings.fix: Tilt down ~12 deg with the phone over 190.03-190.5 so it never leaves frame; land it face-down on his right thigh at (0.56,0.70), navy case back with the cracked corner up, his hand resting on it (ruling S062+: it stays there until S072). Ramp the screen light 1->0 over 4 frames ending exactly 190.6. Cut the reading-lamp spill on the sill by ~1.5 stops and keep the pale window pillar out of frame or in shadow so the last frame sits at mean <=20/255 with only harbour points and a warm lamp edge from frame left. Model the flip cover (open, hinged left) and drop the chrome bezel. Thumb hovers 5-8 mm above the dial key at 188.71, withdraws at 190.03.

findings.issue: T19 match: positions are close but the cut jumps ~2 stops: S058 ends at mean 9/255 (shoulders barely above black), S059 opens at 40 with cream window frames as the brightest elements. The guard's back is ~25% wider (shoulders ~37% of frame width vs 29%) and centred ~0.04 right of the register (0.66,0.50).
findings.fix: S059 side: 75 -> 65 mm or dolly back 0.3 m so shoulder width is ~30% at (0.66,0.50); darken the window frames (dark painted timber, or 1 stop less lamp spill) so frame 0 sits at mean ~22-25; keep the two warm points near (0.52,0.38) to rhyme with S058's candles. S058 (chapel) last 0.5 s: add blue-hour fill so the dove-grey shoulders read at ~0.25 luminance (mean ~20) instead of near-black.

findings.issue: At 187.3 ('手机冷光亮起') nothing visible happens on him; by the end only a faint glint on the hand - the 6500K glow that must rim his right cheek, ear and glasses from below is missing, so the beat that S060/S061 pay off is weak. The thermos (set-up for the S077 refill) is not in frame. The harbour through the window is a flat navy plane with two points (no breakwater, no anchored-ship lights). His hair reads as a white bald cap.
findings.fix: Add a small 6500K area light at the phone, ramping 0->1 over 187.3-187.7, aimed up to rim cheek/ear/glasses rim (screen face never visible). Place the dented steel thermos with its scuffed navy cup-lid at lower right ~(0.86,0.82). Add 8-12 harbour light points at varied depth plus a breakwater lamp line. Hair: short salt-and-pepper texture with darker temples, thinning crown.

findings.issue: The film's emotional core does not land. S062 f4680: she enters at screen-left almost invisible (only two steaming cups read); the guard is cropped at the right edge. From ~196.0 s she kneels on the bench behind him and leans ~40 deg across his back, her right arm passing over his left shoulder to put his cup on the sill BEYOND him (f4718 196.6 s, f4737): it reads as her looming over or embracing him from behind, not 'placing a cup beside him'. S063 (198.22 '坐定', 199.3 unbutton, 200.15 shoulders drop): she ends seated behind him in depth with her torso overlapped by his back, heads at the same height, both lit mannequin faces visible. No 'quiet two-shot with 40 cm between them' ever forms. The button and the shoulder drop are invisible (hands hidden by his body), and 74% of S063's pixels are below 10% grey (mean 8%). Geometry cause: the B3Q camera (1.98,1.45,2.08) looks NNE along a bench that runs N-S, parallel to the east pane. The guard-restorer axis is ~28 deg off the lens axis, so 0.62 m of spacing projects to ~0.29 m and the two bodies stack.
findings.fix: Keep the BAY_3Q sense (guard screen-right by the east window, she screen-left) but swing the camera west so the lens axis is ~55 deg off the bench line. S062: dolly (1.20,1.40,1.55) -> (1.35,1.38,1.30), 40 mm, looking at the pair midpoint (3.23,0.95,0.0). The heads then separate to ~x 0.38 / 0.64 with clear air between them, the lamp sits at upper left and the window fills the back. Re-stage the hand-over beside him, not over him. She stops standing at the north end of HER seat (no knee on the bench), turns ~30 deg toward him and sets his cup on the sill in front of the gap between the seats (move CUP_G to z ~ +0.02, hers 6 cm north). Arm reach <= 0.55 m, torso lean <= 0.3 rad, and her arm never crosses his shoulder line. Cup down on '手' 197.15. S063 locked on the S062 end position: she sits on her own seat on the band entry (198.22). Make the unbutton read on the near side: right hand at the middle button 199.0-199.4 with a 2 cm drop of the coat front. Make 200.15 a visible 3-4 cm clavicle/shoulder drop on both. Light: a moon-silver rim on her from the corridor doors through 196.0 (moonEdge >= 1.0) so the entry reads in the first 0.5 s. Exposure +0.5 stop (target mean >= 12%, <= 50% of pixels under 10%). Keep both faces turned toward the window/each other so the NE lamp only rims their far cheeks and no full face plane is presented to the lens.

findings.issue: Director note #1 (S065 named) is NOT fixed, and the beat inverts. The brief's 'he looks up, she nods, both breathe out' is shot from behind-left. When he looks up at her (202.9, f4874->f4884) his face turns AWAY from the lens and we see the back of his grey hair cap: it reads as him turning from her. Her face is the brightest object in frame, a fully lit frontal-3/4 mannequin mask (sculpted closed lids, mouth line, jagged hair-cap edge at the forehead). The nod at 203.5 and the exhale at 203.9 do not read. The two heads overlap in depth (his nearer and larger), so this is not the 'clean, direct two-shot' the shot list asks for.
findings.fix: Move the camera directly behind the pair on the west side: ~(1.75,1.18,0.05), 75 mm, looking east at (3.23,1.12,0.0), heads at (0.36,0.42) and (0.64,0.44) against the dark window with harbour bokeh. Both are then in lost profile. He lifts his head and turns 35-40 deg north toward her: his face turns INTO the NE reading lamp, which gives a warm 3/4 rim on his far cheek and a catch-light cue at the eye socket, so the look reads through the turn and light, not through the mask. She turns ~30 deg south and nods (6-8 deg chin dip, 0.4 s down / 0.5 s up, peak on 203.5). Kill all frontal fill on her face (cheek >= 1.5 stops under his rim) and set f/2 on the eye-line. Exhale at 203.9: a visible 2-3 cm shoulder drop on both. Hold through '千年啊'.

findings.issue: The call does not read and note #1 (S073, S074 named) is NOT fixed. S072 from 227.4 (f5459, f5496): his right palm and the phone are pressed across the NEAR side of his face, covering eyes and nose, so he reads as hiding his face or slapping his forehead. At S072 f0 no hand is in frame (the phone is at the bottom-right edge), so the S071->S072 'raised hand' match cut has nothing to match. S073 (the held breath in the full-band stop): a giant, evenly warm-lit orange mannequin head fills the right 60% of frame, eyes are sculpted closed lids, the phone sits under his chin/mouth rather than at the ear, and there is a jagged neck/collar seam at (0.83,0.65). Mean 17% vs 8-10% in S072/S074, a one-stop flash on the quietest beat. S074 (230.63 answered, face eases): his hand covers his face for all 3.3 s, so the brows easing and mouth relaxing cannot be seen. Her face is a lit frontal mask throughout.
findings.fix: Right-ear call on the far side of his head. From BAY_3Q his right ear faces away from the lens, so the phone hand goes there, hidden by his head: only the raised navy elbow and a sliver of the case edge read beyond his head silhouette. Turn his head 15-20 deg toward the window so his left profile is a lost profile against the dark glass. S072: move the lift to 226.29-226.6 so his hand and phone already rise through ~(0.55,0.62) at f0, carrying S071's raised hand (0.50,0.55) across the match cut; add the phone's cool 6500K glow on his fingers. S073: MCU, not a giant head. 100 mm from >= 1.8 m, head <= 35% of frame height, eye at (0.58,0.42), face 3/4-back with the lamp key off. The only light on the face is the phone's cool edge on ear and cheek plus a warm lamp rim from behind; mean ~10% to match the neighbours. Raise the jacket collar ~1 cm to hide the neck seam. S074: the easing reads in silhouette (head lifts ~5 deg, shoulders drop ~3 cm, elbow lowers slightly as he murmurs). Her smile is carried by the cheek line in profile, rim-lit from the window rather than keyed from the front, then the head turn to the window on 233.07.

findings.issue: 'He quietly gives back the warmth she gave' does not read, and the dawn is missing. At 238.26 and 238.97 (f5718, f5735) the thermos is held horizontally at arm's length above the cups like a telescope or flashlight: no tilt, no stream, mouth ~10 cm from the cups. The cap-off at 237.54 does not read. The window is still night-blue with a moonlit sea and harbour lights (mean 18%, RGB 45/45/54), although the shot list says window light becomes key. Faces are keyed from the lamp at screen-left, so the T25 rhyme 'light from screen-right' fails. They keep looking down at the cups until ~239.9 (sync 239.6).
findings.fix: Cap: a visible twist and the cap held in his left hand at 237.54. Pour: thermos tilted 50-60 deg down with its mouth 4-6 cm above her cup on 238.26, a thin warm-brown stream for ~0.3 s, then his cup on 238.97. Lower the camera ~15 cm and pan 5 deg right so the cups and spout sit in clear air beside his arm (~(0.62-0.70,0.62)). Sky: drive DAWN to ~1.0 by 237.1 (pale P20 sky with a thin P21 line over a still-dark sea; harbour lamps on). The east window becomes the key: cool 6500K rim on both profiles from screen-right, lamp down ~50%. Heads lift to the window by 239.6. Also start the paling in S074 (DAWN 0.36 at 233.9 is invisible now) so the S074->S075 'light' cut actually connects a brightening window to the first light at sea.

findings.issue: The brief's 'hands and teacups' close-up has an odd gesture and loses its continuity plants. Her left forearm lies straight and flat along the sill from frame left with the hand palm-up and fingers splayed upward right next to her cup (f4816-f4864), which reads as begging, reaching for the cup, or a lifeless arm on a bar counter. His hands enter cut off by the top frame edge and leave UP and right (f4840) instead of 'lifted toward his lap, out of frame low right'. The worn cuff spot (the film's clearest plant, registered at (0.42,0.62)) does not read at 960 px: the cuff is a uniform dark tube. Neither cup shows the cobalt line or the 2 o'clock chip (in S063 the line renders as a dotted, aliased ring).
findings.fix: Keep the palm-up geometry (it is what turns the ulnar cuff side to this lens) but make it a resting hand. Elbow off the sill: only the wrist and the back of the hand rest on the sill edge, forearm angled in from lower-left at ~30 deg, fingers curled ~1.0 into a soft half-closed hand ~6 cm from her cup, not touching it. Add a grazing warm kick across the cuff so the 18x8 mm abrasion reads at least 0.5 stop lighter than the cloth, with 100 mm focus on it at 201.6. His hands: frame them fully at f0 (camera tilt down ~4 deg) and drive the lift path down-right (y increasing) out of frame low right by 202.3. Cups: thicken the cobalt band to ~2 mm or use aa 'msaa' for S062-S064, and turn his cup so the chip sits on the visible rim at 2 o'clock.

findings.issue: The last image is close but loses two of its own requirements. His (right) cup's steam column rises in front of the brightest SE pane, so it nearly disappears (the shot list says steam backlit against the dark muntin / NE pane, never the brightest sky). The left column works. At sill height the rims are edge-on, so the 2 o'clock chip that identifies his cup cannot be seen. The reflected pair in the NE pane are two orange blobs at (0.12,0.3)/(0.32,0.3) that read as smudges more than 'two people sitting'.
findings.fix: Shift the camera ~4 cm left (or both cups 3 cm left) so the centre muntin sits behind the right cup's steam and the left column has the dark NE pane behind it. Raise the camera ~3 cm so the rims open to a slight ellipse, and turn his cup so the chip is a notch on the rim silhouette at 2 o'clock. Reflections: cooler and darker head-and-shoulders silhouettes (she left, he right as in S063) at ~25% opacity, with less orange saturation.

findings.issue: The cut into S061 is built on 'the phone light dies, she sees only the dark bent back', but S060's last frame (f4582) shows a warm-lit hand floating over a bright cream sill and jamb with the phone gone (endframe: phone face-down on his right thigh, cracked corner visible, lit only by the lamp and harbour points). It is 1 stop brighter (mean 17%) than S061 f0 (8%), so the darkness does not carry across the cut.
findings.fix: End S060 on the shot list's endframe: the phone face-down on his right thigh (0.56,0.70) under his resting hand, the sill out of frame or flagged, lit only by the 2700K lamp edge. Drop exposure ~0.8 stop over the last 0.4 s (190.6-190.96) as the screen light dies, so the cut lands dark into dark.

findings.issue: T18 set-up fails: the clear diamond quarry at (0.70,0.45) with the restorer's half-seen face is unreadable - it is lost among large, saturated, defocused foreground petals as one more pale blob. The brief's '修复师的倒影在一小块玻璃里若隐若现' and the S057<->S061 'same glass, seventy years apart' rhyme both depend on this shot.
findings.fix: Make the quarry the clearest shape on the right third: a thin candle glint on its lead cames outlining the lozenge, clear glass darker than its coloured neighbours (dark nave behind), the face inside as a cool moon-silver (temp -0.3 against the warm chapel) low-ponytail silhouette at 12-15% luminance, fading in 180.94->182.4. Darken/desaturate the surrounding foreground petals ~30% and halve their scale; bias focus so the quarry's CoC is <=3 px while the profile stays sharp.

findings.issue: Mid-crane (~176.0) the frame is ~85% flat lime wall crossed by streaky, noisy shafts, the lancet cut at the right edge and a black-and-white striped object at the left edge (x<0.07) that reads as an artefact; for ~1.5 s the 'grand and quiet' volume (vault, nave depth) disappears. Frame 0 lancet is narrower (x 0.66-0.78) with its top visible rather than cut.
findings.fix: Move the crane path 2.5-3 m off the south wall and start the 40 deg pan by 175.4 so vault ribs, the nave and the shafts' landing on the floor stay in frame through the descent; remove/fix the striped object; increase shaft samples (or blue-noise jitter) so dust reads as dust, not scratches. Frame 0: lancet x 0.62-0.92 with its top cut by the frame as written.

findings.issue: MOTHER's costume reads as a white short-sleeved shirt with a turn-down collar and front buttons (modern blouse / T-shirt) rather than the dove-grey qipao with a stand collar - the 1950s Nanyang era cue is lost, and white cloth blooms under the petals (S058 at 185.1).
findings.fix: Dove-grey qipao (mid-grey ~0.45 albedo, slight sheen): mandarin stand collar, diagonal right-side placket with 2-3 frog buttons, cap sleeves; the petals then read as coloured light on grey silk without clipping.

findings.issue: The third act of kindness is murky and does not set up the S070 textile dissolve. Mean 12%; the subjects (two backs at x 0.25-0.60) are dim blue-grey, while the brightest area is an empty candle-lit wall in the right third (x 0.75-1.0) that pulls the eye away. A dark pew back occupies the bottom third. Shot from behind, 'his hands on the old cap loosen a little' cannot be seen. The shot never 'stops on the two sleeves side by side': it stays an MS of two backs, so at the dissolve the sleeves are ~10% of frame height against S070's planned 30% cuff. f0 has her standing still with hands clasped, so the 'downward motion' match from S068 has no motion at the cut.
findings.fix: Re-frame 3/4 from behind-left at 75 mm, lower (eye 1.1 m), and push in ~10% over the 2 s. At 219.24 the touching sleeves (her short dove-grey, his thin white cotton) fill the lower centre, with the contact at (0.42,0.62) and the sleeve band ~30% of frame height (the A frame for S070's cuff macro). Light: a cool clerestory top light on shoulders and sleeves (+1 stop on the figures), flag the candle wall down ~1 stop, target mean ~15%. Open on her last step already lowering into the seat (hips descending by f0+6) so the cut from S068 carries a downward motion. Show his hands on the cap in his lap past her arm (a 2 cm loosening at 218.9).

findings.issue: Frame 0: the anchor (her lit window at (0.42,0.46), carried over from S017's candle) competes with ~20 equally bright windows in the right half and the moon glitter on the water; the restorer silhouette in the window is not visible. The city windows are uniform in colour and brightness (game-like grid).
findings.fix: For the first 1.0 s dim the right-half city by ~40% (or start closer so her window is ~25% of frame height) and add the tiny bent silhouette against her lamp; vary window colour 2400-3500K and brightness, <=35% lit. Keep the rise and the moon end frame - they work.
